findings.problem: This diff undoes commit 542d5dd almost line for line. The General section is wrapped again in its own <form action=save_settings> with no submit button (lines 18-90). The only 'Save Settings' button sits in the second, id-less <form action=save_settings> at line 134. The form="settings-form" association is removed. The file already uses the form-attribute approach to avoid nested forms elsewhere: the add-instance inputs use form="add-{{ app_name }}" (lines 230-232) tied to the out-of-form <form id="add-..."> at line 250. The diff drops that approach for General but keeps it for add-instance.

members.title: Diff reverts a tested fix: General settings silently reset to hardcoded defaults on every instance save
members.problem: This diff reverts commit 542d5dd, reintroducing the bug that commit fixed and tested against. General-section inputs are back in their own standalone <form> (settings.html:18-90) with no submit control, and id="settings-form" is stripped from the instances form (settings.html:134) along with every form="settings-form" attribute. Clicking 'Save Settings' (settings.html:241-244) submits solely the instances form; none of the General fields are in that POST. In triggarr/web/routes.py save_settings (lines 530-540), every one of those fields is read via form.get(...) with a hardcoded fallback default, so every routine instance save silently overwrites administrator-configured General settings. tests/test_web.py::test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form (added in 542d5dd) fails against this markup.
members.why_it_matters: Silently discards admin-configured resource/behavior controls (hard_max_per_cycle, request_timeout) on every routine settings save, replacing them with hardcoded defaults without warning.
members.fix_hint: Restore the pre-revert structure from commit 542d5dd: keep General fields in a plain <div> with form="settings-form" on each control, and restore id="settings-form" on the instances <form> that holds the 'Save Settings' button.

members.title: General settings form has no submit button, so edits to General fields can never be saved
members.problem: The diff wraps the General fields in their own <form> (lines 18-90) and removes the form="settings-form" association. That form contains no submit button. The only 'Save Settings' button sits in the second form at lines 134-246. The General form also has many fields, so under the HTML spec pressing Enter does not submit it either. A user who edits log level, hard max, timeouts, page size, tracking window, max failures or skip_unreleased has no way to send those changes. This reverts the fix in commit 542d5dd.
members.why_it_matters: The whole General settings section stops working: any change a user makes is silently thrown away.
members.fix_hint: restore form="settings-form" on the General inputs and id="settings-form" on the instances form (or revert this diff)

members.title: Keep General controls associated with the Save Settings form
members.problem: The new General form ends before the form containing Save Settings and has no submit button. Removing the explicit form associations means clicking Save Settings submits only instance fields. save_settings (triggarr/web/routes.py:531-539) interprets missing General fields as defaults, then persists them at lines 608-612. For example, an existing hard_max_per_cycle=10 becomes 0 (unlimited), skip_unreleased=true becomes false, and max_history_rows=10000 becomes 1000. General edits are also discarded.
members.why_it_matters: Save Settings now omits every General field and silently overwrites saved configuration with defaults.
members.fix_hint: Restore id="settings-form" on the submitting form and form="settings-form" on every General control. Verify the existing test_general_fields_submit_with_the_save_settings_form regression test passes.

members.title: Reverts the 542d5dd fix: every 'Save Settings' click silently resets all General settings to their defaults
members.problem: This diff brings back exactly the bug HEAD commit 542d5dd fixed. The General controls are wrapped in their own <form action=save_settings> again (lines 18-90) with no submit button. The only 'Save Settings' button sits in the separate instances form at line 134, which no longer has id="settings-form". Clicking Save posts only the instance fields. In triggarr/web/routes.py save_settings (:520-540), each missing General field is filled with its fallback and skip_unreleased becomes False. These values pass validation and are written to config.toml. Any custom General value is lost on every save, and skip_unreleased flips from True to False so the daemon starts searching unreleased items. The regression test tests/test_web.py:833-890 will fail.
members.why_it_matters: Loses persisted configuration silently on every settings save, affecting every user of the settings page. Flipping skip_unreleased to False changes search behavior against Radarr, Sonarr and Lidarr.
members.fix_hint: Discard this working-tree change: restore id="settings-form" on the instances form, put form="settings-form" back on every General control, and keep the General section in a plain <div>.

findings.title: Save Settings now posts without General fields, so the handler resets every General setting to its default
findings.problem: After the diff, the instances form (line 134) no longer carries the General fields. save_settings (routes.py:529-540) builds the whole 'general' config from form.get(...), using hard-coded fallbacks when a field is missing. Every 'Save Settings' click therefore writes: log_level='info', hard_max_per_cycle=0, max_history_rows=1000, request_timeout=30, page_size=50, tracking_window_minutes=60, max_consecutive_failures=5. skip_unreleased becomes False because form.get('skip_unreleased') == 'on' is False when the field is absent, flipping the default of True (config.py:114) and making the engine search unreleased movies (engine.py:401). This happens even when the user only changed an instance field.
findings.fix_hint: keep id="settings-form" here and form="settings-form" on the General inputs so both sections post together
findings.why_it_matters: Saving an instance quietly overwrites the user's General configuration on disk, including turning skip_unreleased off, which changes how searches run.
